DOA Policy: What to Do if Livestock Arrives Dead
body:
If your coral or fish arrives dead on arrival (DOA):

1. Take photos immediately - Photograph the animal in the unopened bag
2. Contact the seller within 2 hours of delivery. If they have DOA policy that allows for returns
3. Keep all packaging as proof
4. File a claim through the Reef Market order system

Most sellers offer full refund or store credit for legitimate DOA claims. Always check the seller's specific DOA policy before purchasing.

title: Understanding Water Chemistry Basics
body:
Key parameters for a healthy reef:

- Salinity: 1.025-1.026 sg
- Temperature: 76-78°F
- Alkalinity: 7-9 dKH
- Calcium: 400-450 ppm
- Magnesium: 1300-1400 ppm
- Nitrate: < 10 ppm (some is actually beneficial)
- Phosphate: 0.03-0.1 ppm

Consistency is more important than hitting exact numbers!

title: Beginner's Guide to Starting a Reef Tank
body:
Starting a reef tank is an exciting journey! Here's what you need to know:

1. Choose the right tank size - A 40 gallon breeder is ideal for beginners
2. Get quality equipment - Invest in a good protein skimmer and lighting
3. Cycle your tank - This takes 4-6 weeks. Be patient!
4. Start with hardy corals - Mushrooms, zoanthids, and GSP are great first corals
5. Test your water regularly - Ammonia, nitrite, nitrate, alkalinity, calcium, and magnesium

Remember: nothing good happens fast in a reef tank!

title: How to Acclimate New Corals
body:
When receiving shipped corals:

1. Float the bag in your tank for 15 minutes to temperature acclimate
2. Open the bag and add a small amount of tank water every 5 minutes for 30 minutes
3. Use a coral dip (like Bayer or CoralRx) before placing in your tank
4. Place the coral in a low-flow, low-light area initially
5. Gradually move to its permanent position over 1-2 weeks

⚠️ Never pour shipping water into your tank!
